description: A recorder in the signal path: it copies its input to its output until you capture a stretch of that input and play the capture back instead

params.text: rec button — press to start a capture and press again to end it; starting one throws away the previous capture and stops playback
play button — press to play the capture from its beginning; pressing during playback restarts it, and with no capture stored it does nothing
Press to end playback, after which out returns to copying the input

inputs.text: The signal captured and played back, and the signal copied to out at every moment when no capture is playing
rec input — a rise above 1V starts a capture and the next one ends it; starting a capture throws away the previous one and stops playback
play input — a rise above 1V plays the capture from its beginning, and a second rise part way through restarts it; with no capture stored it does nothing

outputs.text: The capture while it is playing, and a copy of the input at every other moment; when the capture runs out playback ends and the copy resumes

notes: the module holds no capture when it is added to a patch, and play does nothing until one exists. Start a capture with the rec button or a rise on the rec input, and end it the same way.
a capture holds 192000 samples. That is four seconds at a 48kHz sample rate, two at 96kHz, and the capture ends by itself on reaching the limit.
playback advances by one stored sample for each sample of the engine, so a capture made at one sample rate plays back faster or slower after the rate is changed.
the capture is held in memory only. It is not written into the patch file and is gone when the patch is closed.
the output takes its channel count from the input jack rather than from the capture, so a polyphonic capture played back with the input unplugged produces no channels at all.
the three red lamps show, from the top, that a capture is running, that playback is running, and that the stop button is held down.
